issues.legal_issue: A party cannot challenge in an appeal from a final decree an issue conclusively determined by an earlier preliminary decree that became final.
material_facts: The trial court's preliminary decree held that the earlier deposit and proceedings to obtain release of the mortgaged property did not prevent the suit for accounts.

The High Court affirmed that determination in an earlier appeal. Although a certificate to appeal was refused, the appellants did not seek special leave to appeal, and the High Court judgment became final.
The appellants sought to raise the maintainability issue in an appeal from the later final decree.
issues.conclusion: The appellants could not reopen the maintainability issue in the appeal from the final decree because it had been determined by the preliminary decree, which had become final.
issues.legal_principle: A preliminary decree in an accounts suit finally determines the issues decided at that stage; it is not merely interlocutory. A party seeking to challenge such a determination must pursue an available appeal from it, and cannot revive the issue in an appeal from the final decree after the earlier decision has become final.

predicates.appeal_from_final_decree: A party brings an appeal from a final decree in a proceeding after the issue was addressed at an earlier stage.
predicates.earlier_decree_resolved_the_issue: The earlier decree determined the issue now raised in the later appeal.
predicates.earlier_decree_became_final: The earlier decree was affirmed or otherwise became final without a successful further appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a final decree concerns an issue already resolved by an earlier decree that became final, the issue cannot be reopened.

issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgagee who is not entitled to take all property receipts in lieu of interest and remains entitled to interest when the property produces no receipts must render accounts of the property.
material_facts: The mortgagee took possession of the mortgaged property.
The mortgage terms entitled the mortgagee to a fixed monthly sum in lieu of interest, rather than all receipts from the property.
The mortgagors remained liable for interest when the property was vacant or the mortgagee could not collect rents.
The mortgagee could increase rents or replace a tenant, but could appropriate only the fixed monthly sum toward interest, not the entire increased rent.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage did not fall within the category described in section 77 of the Transfer of Property Act; section 76 applied, and the mortgagee was liable to account for the administration of the property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 76 and 77 of the Transfer of Property Act distinguish between a mortgagee in possession who must account for the property's administration and the specified mortgage arrangement to which section 77 applies. The terms of the mortgage govern that classification; where the mortgagee's entitlement is not confined to the property's receipts and does not extend to all increased rents, section 77 does not apply and the duty to account under section 76 applies.

predicates.usufructuary_mortgage_accounting_case: The proceeding concerns accounting for a property held by a mortgagee under a usufructuary mortgage.
predicates.mortgagee_took_possession: The mortgagee took possession of the mortgaged property.
predicates.mortgagee_was_not_entitled_to_all_proper: The mortgage terms limited the sums the mortgagee could take toward interest instead of giving the mortgagee all receipts from the property.
predicates.interest_remained_payable_without_proper: The mortgagor remained liable for interest during periods when the property produced no receipts or the mortgagee could not collect rent.

issues.definition: If an accounting proceeding concerns a usufructuary mortgage, the mortgagee took possession, was not entitled to all property receipts as interest, and remained entitled to interest without property receipts, the mortgagee must render accounts.

issues.legal_issue: The Usurious Loans Act does not apply to a suit solely for accounts and a surplus where the reliefs constituting redemption have already been obtained and the relevant security was created before the Act came into force in the area.
material_facts: The mortgagors' transferee deposited money under section 83 of the Transfer of Property Act, and the mortgagee accepted it, delivered possession of the property and the relevant documents, and received payment.

The later suit sought accounts of the mortgagee's administration and payment of any surplus; it did not seek delivery of the mortgage deed or other documents, possession, or retransfer of the property.
The security was created in 1933, when the Usurious Loans Act did not apply in the area; the Act was applied there later.

The High Court applied the Usurious Loans Act to grant additional relief, and the Supreme Court held that the suit did not qualify under the Act's categories for redemption or enforcement of an agreement in respect of a loan.
issues.conclusion: The Usurious Loans Act did not apply to the suit, and the mortgagors were not entitled to relief under it.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(3)(b) and (c) of the Usurious Loans Act, the relevant suit must be one for enforcement of an agreement in respect of a loan or for redemption of a security, and the relevant agreement must have been made or security given after commencement of the Act. Under section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, a suit for redemption enforces the right to obtain the mortgage documents, possession where applicable, and retransfer or extinguishment of the mortgagee's interest. A suit solely for accounts and a surplus is not thereby a redemption suit or a suit to enforce an agreement. Section 3(3) of the Usurious Loans Act addresses the form of a suit and does not remove section 2(3)'s timing requirements. Under sections 3(13) and 5(3) of the General Clauses Act, commencement is when the Act comes into force in the relevant area, not merely when it comes into operation elsewhere. The Court relied on Gajambal Ramalingam v. Rukn-ul-Mulk Syed Abdul Wajid and Re Hayes on the area's status, and rejected the contrary interpretation in Vaishnu Dass v. Thaker Dass.

rule.if: mortgage_accounting_suit and suit_seeks_only_accounts_and_surplus and redemption_reliefs_already_obtained and security_predates_local_applicability

predicates.mortgage_accounting_suit: The proceeding is a suit by a mortgagor seeking accounts of a mortgagee's administration of mortgaged property.
predicates.suit_seeks_only_accounts_and_surplus: The suit seeks accounts and any resulting surplus, rather than relief enforcing redemption or an agreement in respect of a loan.
predicates.redemption_reliefs_already_obtained: Before the suit, the mortgagee accepted a deposit and delivered the relevant documents and possession, so the mortgagor had already obtained the reliefs constituting redemption.
predicates.security_predates_local_applicability: The security was created before the relevant law became applicable in the area where the property was situated.

issues.definition: When a mortgage accounting suit seeks only accounts and a surplus, redemption reliefs have already been obtained, and the security predates local applicability, relief under the Usurious Loans Act is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on an amount already payable when a suit is instituted may run from the institution of the suit.
material_facts: The amount decreed as the surplus, after excluding relief under the Usurious Loans Act, was payable by the mortgagee when the suit was instituted.
The High Court allowed interest on that amount from the date the suit was instituted, and the Supreme Court rejected the request to start interest only from the High Court's decree.
issues.conclusion: Interest on the amount found due was payable from the date the suit was instituted.
issues.legal_principle: Because the amount decreed was already payable when the suit was instituted, the Court found no error in allowing interest from that date rather than from the date of the later decree.

predicates.mortgage_surplus_claim_suit: The proceeding seeks payment of a surplus found due from a mortgagee after accounting.
predicates.amount_was_payable_when_suit_was_filed: The amount later decreed was already payable by the defendant when the plaintiff instituted the suit.

issues.definition: If a suit seeks a mortgage surplus and the amount was payable when the suit was filed, interest runs from the filing of the suit.
